title: Quantile-aware token-latency observable playground and conditional failover tuning
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Implement a quantile-aware token-latency observability pipeline and a set of exploratory dashboards that enable ops and SREs to tune conditional multi-region failover thresholds. This ticket builds the sampling/aggregation strategy (per-token and per-sequence quantiles), an efficient storage rollup scheme, dashboard panels for p50/p95/p99/p999 by model/region/route, and a small synthetic-harness to exercise degradations and validate failover triggers. The goal is to provide deterministic, low-cost signal for conditional circuit-breaker decisions without instrumenting every token at full-fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end telemetry from ingress to decode with token-quantile rollups (p50,p95,p99,p999) available in metrics store for 30d
Dashboard with model x region x route panels that surface quantile drift, entropy of token latencies, and admission rates
Sampling overhead under 3% CPU and 5% network egress on prod-like load during the 1M tokens/min synthetic test
Failover rule prototypes that trigger conditional region failover when p99 token latency exceeds configured baseline by X% and sustained for Y seconds
Playbook entry documenting how ops should interpret quantile spikes vs KV cache misses and steps to validate false positives
tasks: Design: finalize quantile bucketing scheme (fixed vs t-digest) and retention/rollup policy
Instrumentation: add lightweight token-latency sampler to ingress and decoder stages
Pipeline: implement daily rollup job and realtime streaming aggregator for short-window SLOs
Dashboard: build Grafana dashboard panels and alert rules for quantile drift and admission-impact correlation
Chaos: extend synthetic traffic harness to inject KV miss and slow-decode to validate failover thresholds
Docs + Playbook: write runbook and update SLO design doc with new conditional failover semantics
PRs: implement prod-safe feature flag gating and roll out to canary region
comments: 2026-02-28 - Aisha Kaur: Created initial ticket after SRE sync. Motivation: ops keep seeing short-lived p99 spikes that don't surface in token-avg metrics. Need quantile-first approach to avoid blind failovers.

2026-03-02 - Miguel Santos: Proposed using t-digest for high cardinality token distributions + fixed-size per-shard sketch to bound memory. Raised tradeoff of merge accuracy vs CPU. Posted design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quantile+Token+Observability
2026-03-04 - Design review (Emily Chen): Ask to show example dashboards with synthetic injects and include a panel for 'KV hit ratio vs p99' to disambiguate cache vs decode issues

2026-03-05 - Miguel Santos: Prototype aggregator implemented. Early numbers from canary show p99 correlates strongly with decode slow-path; sampling at 1/32 tokens reduces overhead to ~2.1% CPU. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3874
2026-03-07 - SRE feedback (Jon Park): Need guardrail to avoid failover noise — propose requiring sustained drift for 60s and cross-shard confirmation before triggering conditional failover.

2026-03-09 - Miguel Santos: Dashboard panels committed to staging Grafana. Added alert rule draft: 'conditional-failover-candidate' when p99 > baseline*1.5 for 60s and admission-rate degrade > 10%. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-telemetry/pull/612

2026-03-10 - Aisha Kaur: Updated acceptance criteria to include storage retention and overhead targets. Scheduled canary validation 2026-03-16. Next: parameter sweep for sampling factor and t-digest compression settings.
notes: Sampling strategy: default 1/32 tokens, adaptive backoff on CPU > 70% per host
Aggregation: use t-digest with compression 200 for near-realtime windows, materialize fixed histograms for long-term retention
Privacy: token content is never shipped; only encoded latency sketches are emitted
Failover semantics: this ticket prototypes 'conditional failover' candidates; actual automated failovers will be gated behind a separate runbook and safety checks
